Partial dependencies and second normal form

Unit 2 · Week 3 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the normalisation chapter, normalisation-workbook.md, normalisation-answers.md and the normalisation-pack.zip stage datasets. Use fictional data on paper or in a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL setup or student account is required. Keep original copies. Suggested 55-minute timings are flexible. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Partial dependencies and second normal form

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the reservation extension of the equipment desk. These are reservation requests, not issued loans. Keep the earlier Loan datasets unchanged. All activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

2. The key and a borrower’s label

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

BorrowerID alone determines BorrowerLabel under the stated requirements. Cover item and date to demonstrate. A functional dependency means a value or combination determines one value of another attribute under the rules. It describes a data rule, not a physical cause. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

3. What each identifier determines

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

These dependencies come from the exercise rules. BorrowerLabel and equipment facts depend on only parts of the composite reservation key, so the combined register has partial dependencies. ReservationStatus belongs to the whole reservation. CategoryID determines CategoryName, which creates a further chain handled at 3NF. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

4. The partial-dependency test

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher model

Model B001: the label is Learner A, but B001 has several requests with different statuses. In this exercise, 2NF requires 1NF plus removal of partial dependencies of non-key facts on a candidate key. Move those facts into tables with appropriate keys. Do not remove legitimate reservation events. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

5. The three tables at 2NF

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

The Reservation composite key is (BorrowerID, EquipmentID, ReservationDate). BorrowerID and EquipmentID also act as FKs to their parent tables. EquipmentDescription is shortened to Description in this summary only. Equipment still contains CategoryName at this stage. Each split follows the stated dependency. Three borrowers, three equipment items and six reservations remain. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

6. A split to explain

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 4–6. Write field names in relation notation and underline PK attributes, not example values. Equipment fields are EquipmentID, EquipmentDescription, CategoryID and CategoryName. Reservation retains the three-part key and status. Check the stage CSVs only after explaining the split. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

7. A stage still has a problem

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. In these straightforward keys, there is no partial dependency on part of a single-field key, but EquipmentID determines CategoryID and CategoryID determines CategoryName. This transitive chain remains. Adding an ID does not automatically cure all dependency problems. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

8. A fresh borrower label

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

Update the B002 record in Borrower. The reservation key values and event statuses remain with their Reservation rows. Related records retrieve the new label through BorrowerID. The label is stored once for that borrower rather than once per request. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.
